correctness.rationale: The positive pressure root follows from the strictly decreasing Laplace sum over primes. Kac/Abramov inducing and relative entropy identify the unique iid renewal equilibrium with q_t(p)=exp(-t-s(p+1)). Partial summation from the effective prime number theorem gives sum_p exp(-sp)=s^{-1}(L^{-1}+gamma L^{-2}+O(L^{-3})), L=log(1/s); taking logarithms and inverting yields e^{-t}/s=t+log t-gamma+o(1). Differentiating the root and the first-moment Laplace expansion gives rho=s(1+L^{-1}+O(L^{-2})); the variational identity h_max=P+t rho yields the stated constrained entropy. The truncated Laplace expansion gives the fixed-x Palm correction. The size-biased stationary renewal construction and convergence of scaled gaps/central interval give the qualitative stationary Poisson limit. The bundled finite verifier is only a numerical corroboration and does not establish the PNT asymptotic or point-process convergence. The main proof obligations are the stated cutoff estimates and termwise differentiated asymptotics, which are plausible consequences of the effective PNT but are not independently certified here.

value.rationale: Prime gaps are a natural arithmetically sparse set of allowed return lengths. The theorem quantifies their thermodynamic effect through an Euler-constant pressure correction and a constrained entropy deficit, and identifies the rare-marker Poisson scaling with a first arithmetic correction. These are motivated invariants of a natural shift, not arbitrary finite values or a routine substitution.
